title: KPI fidelity checklist and contingency notebook
content:
Purpose:
This notebook is a compact, pragmatic playbook to validate KPI fidelity before and during a launch window and to provide lightweight contingencies when telemetry diverges from expectations. It focuses on signal quality (does the metric mean what we think it means), latency of observability (how quickly we can see failure), and actionable owner-run play steps. Aim: reduce false positives/negatives so ops decisions (throttle, rollback, degrade) are defensible and timely.

Scope and intended users:
- Audience: product-ops, release engineers, SRE oncall, analytics engineer on the launch team.
- Scope: launch-facing KPIs (latency, error-rate, tokens/unit cost, adoption funnels, model-quality regressions), instrumentation checks, runbook triggers, and contingency actions. Not intended to replace full postmortem docs.

How to use this doc (quick workflow):
1) Preflight (T-7d to T-0): run the Instrumentation checklist, synthetic tests, and drift probes.
2) Canary (T0+): start canary, monitor the Decision Thermostat (see below), execute contingency if any gating metric crosses threshold.
3) Ramp: periodic KPI fidelity audits (sample verification, label checks) at 15m cadence during first 24h, then hourly until steady.
4) Post-launch (24–72h): retrospective sample audit, action item bake-off.

INSTRUMENTATION CHECKLIST (preflight)
- Metric definition doc exists and linked (owner: analytics eng). Confirm the precise numerator/denominator.
- Synthetic traffic: run 1k synthetic requests across common routes; assert telemetry reflects requests (check traces and request ids).
- Sampling validation: confirm that sampled logs include both success and failure cases with consistent keys (request_id, model_version, routing_policy).
- Latency buckets: ensure histogram boundaries match SLO buckets (10ms, 50ms, 200ms, 1s, 5s).
- Cost accounting: verify tokenization counts against reference impl for 3 sample prompts (short, medium, long).
- Embedding checks: run deterministic vector test to ensure embedding vector norms in expected range.
- Alert proofing: create test alerts for each critical metric and validate they fire to oncall.
- Dashboard sanity: ensure dashboard refresh interval <= 30s for critical panels.
- Event provenance: confirm every metric has a mapped event source (api-gateway, routing service, runtime) and one-line description in metric registry.

DECISION THERMOSTAT (gating layer)
- Purpose: quick, human-readable snapshot to decide whether to continue ramp, pause, or rollback.
- Core gates (example):
  1) Request success rate (per-route) — Gate: 99.5% over 5m (canary) / 99.0% over 1h (ramp). Owner: SRE.
  2) P50 latency (user-facing) — Gate: <= 250ms 95% of the time (5m). Owner: infra lead.
  3) Token cost drift — Gate: +15% over baseline average for 30m. Owner: product-ops.
  4) Model-quality regression (prompt probe set) — Gate: >3% worse accuracy/acceptance on golden set over 15m. Owner: applied-ml.
  5) Error mix (client vs runtime) — Gate: client errors increasing >> runtime errors (indicates client misconfig). Owner: SDK/devex.

If any single critical gate trips: immediately notify #prod-ops-launch and trigger Contingency A (see below). If multiple gates trip or the triage shows cascading issues, escalate to Incident Commander.

SAMPLE KPIs and FIDELITY CHECKS (short table, interpreted as text)
- latency_p50_ms: validate with trace-level timestamps; sample 50 traces per 10m and assert timestamp alignment.
- success_rate_route_X: cross-check API logs vs runtime logs for same request_ids; discrepancy >0.2% => telemetry bug.
- cost_per_1k_tokens: verify billing pipeline tags model_variant correctly; run manual tokenization and cost calc for 10 sample requests.
- prompt-accept-rate: match automated eval labels to human review on 1% sample; if human/human agreement < 90% — revamp labeling instructions.

CONTINGENCY ACTIONS (lightweight, owner-first)
- Contingency A — Pause and triage (quick):
  - Who: oncall SRE + product-ops owner + analytics engineer.
  - Steps: pause rollout (traffic manager), mark canary -> rollback-route if immediate user impact. Collect 100 request traces and 50 model eval samples.
  - Communication: post concise summary in Slack #prod-ops-launch using template: "PAUSE: [metric] tripped; immediate action: paused ramp; triage owners: @X @Y; initial hypothesis: [one-liner]."
- Contingency B — Degrade gracefully:
  - Use when latency or cost spikes but model quality intact. Route to lower-cost/low-latency model-variant, enable caching for repeated prefixes, increase batching limit temporarily.
- Contingency C — Telemetry repair:
  - When discrepancy found between API and metric registry >0.5% or missing fields. Turn on debug-mode logging for 30m, deploy small patch to metrics pipeline, and run re-ingestion for last 60m of events.
- Contingency D — Quality rollback:
  - If model-quality gate trips: immediately switch to pinned previous model_version; hold rollout and run comparative evaluation on 1k production-sampled prompts.

DECISION LOG TEMPLATE (short entries to append during launch)
- timestamp: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mmZ
- metric: [metric name]
- observed: [value]
- baseline: [value/window]
- action_taken: [pause/reroute/rollback/degrade/none]
- owner: [name]
- notes: [one-sentence reasoning]

SAMPLE ENTRY (example)
- 2025-04-01T14:15Z | model-quality-regression | 4.2% worse vs baseline | baseline 0.0% | action_taken: rollback to v1.14 | owner: Sana Patel | notes: regressed on named-entity prompts; immediate rollback reduced error to baseline.

AUDIT PROCEDURES (post-incident / continuous)
- 1% production-sample audit (first 24h): analytics pulls random stratified sample across user cohorts and routes; applied-ml performs blind labeling on golden tasks.
- Instrumentation RCA checklist: if telemetry discrepancy caused a false alarm, write remediation (schema contract, add unit test, dashboard annotation).
- Alert tuning: for any alert that fired and was a false positive, increase required window or add additional slack metric to avoid similar noise.

OWNER ROSTER AND ESCALATION PATHS
- Product-ops lead: Priya Desai (owner of this doc) — pager: @priyad
- SRE oncall: rotation listed in /confluence/sre/oncall-rota (owner: Marco Alvarez)
- Analytics engineer: Leah Chang — handles metric sampling and registry issues
- Applied ML: Sana Patel — responsible for model quality probes and golden tests
- SDK & Devex: Evan Brooks — handles client-side errors and can patch SDKs quickly

COMMUNICATION CHECKLIST (what to post where)
- Slack immediate: #prod-ops-launch with header "PAUSE/DEGRADE/ROLLBACK — [metric]" and Decision Log link.
- Incident doc: create lightweight incident doc at /confluence/incidents/launch-<shortid>. Include Decision Log entries.
- Customer comms: coordinate with comms/CS only if user-impacting (>0.5% customers affected for >1h).

LAUNCH DAY QUICK-CHECK (T0 to T0+6h):
- 00:00 — confirm synthetic traffic passed in last hour, dashboard green.
- 00:15 — verify sampling aligned; 50 traces checked.
- 01:00 — run 1% human label spot-check, confirm no quality drift.
- 03:00 — cost telemetry sanity check (token counts and billing tags).
- 06:00 — consolidate Decision Log, handoff to day-shift owner.

LIGHTWEIGHT METRIC CONTRACT (for engineers)
- Each metric must have: canonical name, event_source, owner, calc_window, alert_threshold, dashboard_panel_id, doc_link. Store as a single-line CSV row in the metric registry.

OPEN QUESTIONS / NOTES TO SELF
- Evaluate whether we need automated golden-set probing at the edge of routing policy (regional variance).
- Consider pre-registering a small model-variant degrade pool for faster switchovers.
- Add a short unit test in infra-metrics that simulates missing request_id payloads.

Appendix: Useful quick links (to add to linked_artifacts before launch)
- preflight metrics spec (CONF-3612), canary runbook PR (GH #122), oncall rota, alert channel playbook.

End of notebook.
